newNodes.name: Purpose-built granaries
newNodes.emerged: ~9,300 BCE Dhra' (Jordan Valley): raised-floor granaries; sealed storage pits and silos widespread by ~7,000 BCE
newNodes.prereqRationale: Only cultivated grain is stored in bulk; Dhra' granaries belong to the earliest cultivators.
newNodes.desc: Raised floors, sealed pits and mud-plastered bins keep stored grain dry and free of pests, so a harvest lasts until the next one and beyond.
newNodes.distinctFrom: cereal_domesticated changes the plant; this changes how its grain is kept. The granary building has no research requirement; this node improves what granaries hold and how little rots.

newNodes.name: Iron farm tools
newNodes.emerged: ~1,000 BCE Levant (iron sickles, hoes and plough tips); ~600 BCE China; ~500 BCE Ganges plain
newNodes.prereqRationale: Forged bloomery iron applied to the two existing hand tools of tillage and harvest.
newNodes.desc: Forged iron sickles, hoe blades and ploughshares hold an edge and outlast stone and bronze, letting farmers clear forest and work harder soils.
newNodes.distinctFrom: iron_bloomery makes the metal; this puts it into everyday farm tools. Unlike heavy_plough it is a hand-tool and share capability, not a new plough.

newNodes.name: Three-field rotation
newNodes.emerged: ~800 CE Carolingian Francia (estate surveys); widespread in northern Europe by ~1,200 CE
newNodes.prereqRationale: The spring course is legumes and oats; open-field strips are ploughed. A heavy_plough link is often argued but contested, so it is not required.
newNodes.desc: Fields rotate through winter grain, spring legumes or oats, and fallow, so only a third lies idle; oats feed horses and pulses restore the soil.
newNodes.distinctFrom: crop_rotation_norfolk abolishes fallow with fodder roots and clover; this is the earlier regime that halves fallow and adds a spring course.

newNodes.name: Herring buss and sea-curing
newNodes.emerged: ~1,380 CE Low Countries (gutting and salting at sea); ~1,415 CE first herring busses with drift nets
newNodes.prereqRationale: A decked, seaworthy hull for weeks at sea (cog) and salt to cure the catch aboard (salt_extraction).
newNodes.desc: Decked fishing ships stay out for weeks with drift nets, gutting and salting the herring aboard, so the catch reaches distant markets.
newNodes.distinctFrom: fishing_hook is subsistence line fishing; this is an offshore commercial fishery with preservation at sea.

findings: Food lane coverage is front-loaded: 24 of 54 nodes sit in A2, while A4 had a single agriculture node (rotary_quern); iron_farm_tools fills the Iron Age tool step that the tree jumped over.
Only 13 of 54 nodes had a live effect (activity.farming x6, activity.herding x2, caravans x2, courier relay, terraces, oil press); every node now carries a registry operand or live unlock.
activity.farming is an OR of six crops, so only the first completed staple changes anything via the unlock; each crop now also carries its own small, distinct operand so later staples still matter.
Rotation history had a four-Age hole (Neolithic legumes straight to the 1650 Norfolk system); three_field_rotation is the A6 bridge and is proposed as a prerequisite of crop_rotation_norfolk.
Fishing beyond the A1 hook had no research at all although production.outputPerExtractorPerYear covers fishing; herring_buss adds the one commercial-fishery step (A6).

The granary building has no research requirement and no node improved it; grain_storage (A2) gives storage its own causal effects (spoilage, years of demand). Integrators may wish to link the public_granaries civic to it.
harvestVariance.sigmaLogYield draws on nine nodes in this group (sum 0.32 of a 0.6 cap); irrigation nodes in other groups will add to it, so the integrator should watch the cap.

Cost outliers to calibrate: precision_agriculture 94,620 (about four times its Age peers), refrigeration and drip_irrigation 33,450 versus canning and green_revolution 16,730, maize 1,240 versus other A2 staples 310-620, rice_champa 1,480 low for A6.
Dependency changes proposed (4): cereal_domesticated +sickle; pig dog_domestication -> cereal_cultivation; crop_rotation_norfolk +three_field_rotation; heavy_plough iron_bloomery -> iron_farm_tools.
